rules.round_end_condition: deadline expiry or every active object on the board claimed, whichever comes first; claiming the real object never ends the round early

rules.reveal_timing: the real/decoy identity of every claim is withheld from all surfaces until round finalization

authored_content.package_summary: A Nightcap hidden-object hunt: the shared display shows a full illustrated scene, each phone pans an independent viewport into the same coordinate space, and players race to claim objects. Exactly one is real evidence; the rest are decoys drawn from the same investigative-archetype pool. The truth is withheld until one staged reveal at the end.

content.text: The search turned up something that matters. Not everything about it is clear yet, but the room won't be able to un-know that it's there.
The search turned up the piece that actually matters — the room finally has something real to work with, not just a feeling that someone's lying.

surface_contract.phone: pannable viewport into the scene, a minimap showing current position, and the archetype-name list with checkmarks as objects are claimed by anyone
surface_contract.shared_display: the entire scene always visible at once, live unlabeled claim markers, collective progress, and the end-of-round staged reveal
surface_contract.host: progress and fallback visibility without revealing which object is real before the reveal fires

fallback_contract.behavior: If the deadline passes before the real object is claimed, the round finalizes with the reduced clue only. No object's real/decoy status is ever revealed before this point.
fallback_contract.shared_display_line: Six objects. Time's up. Whatever mattered in this room is still in this room.
fallback_contract.host_line: Deadline reached before the real object was claimed. Reduced clue released; advance when ready.
fallback_contract.player_device_line: Time. The room moves on, and so does the case.

resolution_contract.real_object_id: the generated content payload must include a new top-level key real_object_id whose value is exactly one of authored_content.object_slots[].slot_id, chosen because that slot's archetype corresponds to a real, already-resolved fact in this session's case (e.g. pick the murder-weapon slot only if the case's actual weapon fact naturally maps to that archetype); this is a selection among existing authored slots, never an invented new slot
resolution_contract.run_seed: the generated content payload must also include a new top-level key run_seed whose value is a fresh, session-unique string (e.g. incorporate the session or run identifier from session_context) not reused across sessions; the plugin's deterministic slot ordering (which decoys fill the board alongside real_object_id) is keyed on this value, so a repeated or missing run_seed makes every session show the same board composition. This is a stop-gap: the platform-correct fix is for the resolver to stamp a genuinely unique value into resolved_content before generation runs (a resolver.py change affecting every mini-game, out of scope for this package alone), so treat this requirement as load-bearing until that lands, not as a permanent solution.
resolution_contract.real_archetype_source: the identity and clue text for the resolved real evidence object must be drawn from this session's actual generated case data (killer, weapon, motive, etc.) supplied via session_context; the model must never invent case facts independently
resolution_contract.clue_text_source: clues[].content.text is fully authored and does not require generation to fill; it stays deliberately general because per-clue case-specific text generation is not yet supported by the resolver's hybrid-merge (list values are not recursively merged — see engine/mini_games/resolver.py's _merge_into). Case-specific grounding for this round comes entirely through real_object_id (see the real_object_id key above), which the plugin combines with the deterministic object_slots archetype data; deeper per-clue text personalization is a legitimate future enhancement that would require a resolver.py change, out of scope here.
